text: Before the raid, he has a licence to keep. In the Hunter Association lobby, every screen shows a giant holding up a bridge.
Seoa made him wear a white shirt under the vest. Borro folds himself in half to fit through security.
A guard leans in until his nose nearly touches Nib's mask. Nib plays doll.
Then he pokes Nib's cheek, and the uncovered eye twitches dangerously.
Husks aren't supposed to be warm. Jaeha's customer-service smile goes into overdrive.
Nib holds perfectly still while one bead of sweat rolls out from under his mask.
Past the arch, Borro unfolds to his full height like an old man. Jaeha's explanation is even worse.
Mok has a lawyer. Jaeha has two stiff husks. And someone at the back of the gallery is enjoying the show.
A weary Inspector Ryu opens with the night Black Hound left Jaeha to die.
Black Hound's lawyer tells the story Mok once offered Jaeha ten million won to sign: it was the trap-tester's fault.
Then Mok gives a performance: hand on heart, eyes glistening right on cue for the flashes.
In the gallery, Yerin grips the rail until her knuckles go white. She was there.
Asked whether he went in alone, Jaeha bows politely and recites Mok's own rule back to the panel.
Then Choi makes the point Jaeha made at that door, and names who paid for the survey that got it wrong.
He holds up the photo: the iron door, the lamp burning red.
He asks the panel to do the maths on who survived, then drops the market contract in their laps.
The lawyer is on his feet in a second. It's the one subject Black Hound can't afford.
Too late. Every reporter in the room is typing.
Then Yerin takes the stand. Her voice shakes, but every word comes out.
The lawyer smiles kindly and goes straight for the thing she's most ashamed of.
Her eyes fill, and then they steady. She doesn't deny it. She turns it around.
The healer who couldn't move her legs that night stands straight and points right at Mok.
Nobody moves. Every face in the room turns to Mok.
Mok's face holds. His knuckles don't.
In the recess, the shaking catches up with her. Jaeha has Mok's ten-million-won offer recorded, so why not use it?
Because the recording only proves the bribe. Jaeha is after the bigger crime.
Back inside, the panel won't decide on words alone. It wants to see the husks perform, before lunch.
Mok's smile comes back. He knows what Jaeha's husks are: dolls that shatter in traps.
The two husks in question stare straight ahead, sweating.
Noon, in the basement arena: a four-metre construct of granite and brass, an amber core in its chest.
The scanner reads an F-rank summoner. Only Jaeha sees the window underneath: Operator, hidden.
The screen sets the terms: a B-grade opponent, a five-minute limit, and one line of fine print.
He reads it twice. Four years of contracts taught him that one word can be a door.
Without moving his lips, he coaches them on being husks. Borro feels well prepared. Slow is his speciality.
The construct's stone head grinds round, and the clock starts.
Borro marches out like a wind-up toy soldier, far too fast and far too heavy, cracking the floor.
Nib's idea of a husk, it turns out, is a penguin: arms stuck out stiff, flapping at the wrists.
Behind the glass, an evaluator drops his pen, Choi hides his face, and Mok looks very pleased.
The construct swings, and Borro skids back several metres behind his shield, still frozen in his husk pose.
Jaeha flinches once as the blow lands in him too, and keeps his face blank.
He doesn't need to win. He needs one finger in the right place, and he knows whose.
Arms still stuck out, Nib darts straight between the construct's legs. No field form, but still a scout.
He runs up its leg, using the brass bands as rungs.
One finger taps the grille over the core.
The construct freezes mid-swing and goes dark. Nib drops down and snaps back into his husk pose.
Five minutes were allowed. He used four seconds.
Behind the glass, Ryu's glasses slide down his nose, and Mok's smile sets into a grimace.
Jaeha bows to the window like a waiter presenting the bill.
The lawyer is furious. Ryu just holds up the rule sheet. Somebody finally read it.
By lunchtime it's official: licence kept, and Nib and Borro on the books as his husks.
In the corridor, Mok congratulates him for the cameras and mentions Saturday. Jaeha answers like the old trap rat.
Mok squeezes his shoulder hard enough to crease the vest. Jaeha's hand hangs perfectly relaxed.
Behind him, Nib's hand drifts toward his knives.
Without looking round, Jaeha closes a hand over Nib's wrist. He has a better place in mind.
Outside, fans crowd the steps with a cardboard cut-out of a big husk. Nib stares. Borro waves shyly.
Bomi has it all on camera, and her chat is already putting it in the record books.
Nib flapping, Borro marching, Jaeha behind them with his face in his hands. Somehow, it worked.
Choi hands him a coffee, serious for once. He has doubts about Saturday. Jaeha has none.
Then Jaeha stops, as if he can feel someone watching him.
Inside, the woman from the gallery leans on a pillar, arms folded, smiling at him through the glass.
She gives him a tiny wave.
He knows that face. She backed out of the boss room that night with her crossbow up, right beside Mok.
In her palm sits a small brass compass with a glowing violet needle, swinging.
It slows, and settles, trembling, loosely toward the steps.
Straight at Jaeha. Whatever that needle is made to find, it has found him.
